The Fighter
Three And Oh.
Just Getting Started.

Brent Mayol is a 24-year-old undefeated professional boxer — 3–0 — who trains out of Legacy Gym on the Central Coast.

He fights in one of the lightest divisions in the sport, and that changes everything about how a career is built. At his weight, the best opposition, the best sparring and most of the opportunities sit overseas rather than at home.

That's why the start of this year took him to the Philippines — training alongside some of the country's best fighters and spending a month in camp with one of its most respected gyms and coaches. He's back building on that now, and looking for the year-round backing to keep chasing it.

Training Overseas
A Month In The Philippines

Earlier this year Brent spent the start of the season in the Philippines, training alongside some of the country's best fighters and putting in almost a month in camp at Villamor Boxing Gym — one of the country's most respected gyms and coaching teams.

For a fighter in his division, camps like this are where the real work happens — world-class sparring at his weight, and the kind of experience you can't get at home. It's the level Brent is chasing, and the level he needs to keep getting back to.

The Road Ahead

Camp Starts Now.
The Ring Is Overseas.

Brent's next fight won't happen at home. He has been offered a bout overseas — Turkey or Japan — with the venue and date still being finalised between promoters. That's the target, and the work toward it starts now.

The plan is simple and it runs in three stages. Camp opens at Legacy. From there the aim is to place Brent into Japan for invited sparring — real rounds at his weight against fighters he cannot find in Australia. Then he's sharp, tested and ready the moment a date is confirmed.
